name: Los Alamos National Laboratory, LANSCE (Technical Area 53)
notes: Overpass (overpass-api.de and lz4.overpass-api.de) refused essentially every connection attempt for LANL/ORNL after the SLAC extract succeeded (TCP connection refused, then HTTP 429, then connection refused again); overpass.kumi.systems and overpass.osm.ch both answered but returned zero elements even for known-good queries and were dropped as likely partial/regional mirrors. maps.mail.ru/osm/tools/overpass/api/interpreter, suggested mid-session, did return real, complete data: a 1,817-element extract of the wider Los Alamos townsite (streets, apartments, generic industrial buildings, none named or tagged in any way suggesting LANSCE), and a tight 700 m box directly around the LANSCE node itself came back with zero building ways. TA-53's accelerator/experimental core is therefore genuinely almost unmapped in OpenStreetMap, not merely unreached this session. Nominatim's /search and /lookup endpoints were reachable throughout and are the source of the one point drawn on this map.

TA-53 is a security-sensitive area of Los Alamos National Laboratory: per the research brief, only accelerator/experimental areas shown on public LANSCE maps may be depicted, never fences or gates. No fence, gate or access-control feature is drawn or was found.

summary.plain: Los Alamos National Laboratory's LANSCE accelerator area (Technical Area 53) in the hills of northern New Mexico, shown here as a single located point: public geodata for the 800-metre linac and its experimental areas was not available this session.
summary.technical: One local map for facility:los-alamos-national-laboratory. Only OpenStreetMap node 8041862150 ('LANSCE') was locatable this session; the 800 m side-coupled-cavity linac (accelerator:lansce) and the LSND detector's position are both unlocated, for lack of a public, sufficiently precise source.

unlocated.backlog: Look for a public LANSCE facilities brochure or environmental-assessment site plan with a scale bar and at least three identifiable surveyed control points to georeference against; OpenStreetMap itself is confirmed (via maps.mail.ru's working mirror) to carry no building footprints at all within 700 m of the LANSCE point, so a further Overpass retry alone will not help without new contributed OSM data.
unlocated.reason: LANSCE's 800 m side-coupled-cavity linac (src:geo-lanl-linac-page: 'The third and longest stage of the accelerator (800m) is the side-coupled-cavity linac') has no OpenStreetMap trace: a 700 m box directly around the LANSCE point returned zero building ways via a working Overpass mirror, and Nominatim search for 'LANSCE Linac', 'Area A', 'Lujan Neutron Scattering Center' and 'Weapons Neutron Research' each returned zero results. TA-53 is also security-sensitive, so only a public, officially-shown accelerator path would be drawn even if found. The general facility area is drawn via geometry:lansce-site-marker.

unlocated.backlog: Find a LANSCE/LAMPF-era civil-engineering drawing or the original LSND proposal's site plan giving Line A's/Area A's beamline heading and the A6 beam stop's coordinates or its distance and bearing from a surveyed LANSCE control point.
unlocated.reason: LSND's own NIM paper places it about 30 m from the A6 proton beam stop (src:lsnd-nim-1997-detector-paper), and a separate 2020 paper on LANSCE's Area A places a (different, later-proposed) target 'near the center of Area A, some 100 m downstream of the end of the 800-MeV accelerator' (src:geo-lanl-fpns-area-a-nim-2020) -- but the 800-MeV accelerator's own end point is not itself located this session (see accelerator:lansce, above), and no source gives the switchyard/Line-A bend's heading, so a derived point would rest on an unsourced direction, not a sourced one. LSND is therefore left undrawn rather than guessed; the detector-hosting site itself (site:lanl-lansce) is drawn.
